summary: This bill establishes new work requirements for individuals receiving benefits under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and Medicaid, by narrowing exemptions for certain age groups and caregivers, and by requiring able-bodied adults to work, perform community service, or participate in a work program for at least 80 hours per month to maintain eligibility.

scores.thoughts: This bill establishes work requirements for individuals to receive Medicaid benefits, which would likely reduce the number of people eligible for public healthcare. This directly impacts the accessibility and scope of public healthcare programs.

The bill introduces stricter work requirements for both the Food and Nutrition Act (SNAP) and Medicaid, aiming to reduce dependency on these programs. This directly aligns with reducing welfare spending and tightening access to social safety net programs.

The bill includes an exemption from work requirements for individuals participating in a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation program. While not a primary focus, this provision tangentially relates to drug policy by acknowledging and accommodating treatment efforts within the context of social programs.
